justification: fetch_dcp_setbacks is the one guarded read behind every served numeric DCP control. Its registry link-map query raised on every call and the except swallowed it, so every number has been served without a PDF citation link since 2026-08-26 - a silent wrong output on the served path.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: any parameterised execute() literal in scripts/, services/, src/ or enrichment/ holds a bare % (not %s, %(name)s or %%), or fetch_dcp_setbacks run through a cursor that %-formats parameterised SQL returns an empty registry_pdf_urls map
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Run against origin/main's two files (bb4a463d) with the working tree untouched: the fetch_dcp_setbacks check logged 'fetch_dcp_setbacks registry pdf map: %o format: an integer is required, not str' and returned registry_pdf_urls {}; the scan returned conveyancing_db.py:519 '...discarded 60% of them.' and build_lot_search_index.py:144 '+45% in Sydney' and '79% of lots'. With the fix: 182 passed across the new file and test_conveyancing_db, test_dcp_as_at, test_dcp_controls_api, test_conveyancing_dcp_needs_review, test_lot_search.

pre_impl.existing_data: Measured 2026-09-13: GET https://verify.plotdetect.com.au/api/dcp/structured-controls returned pdf_url null for every control across penrith (12), hornsby (19), campbelltown (9), ku_ring_gai (5) and waverley (10), although 40 of those 55 carry a pdf_page. The same SQL on the production database raised IndexError('tuple index out of range') with the comment and returned 2 rows for penrith without it. git blame: the comment arrived in 188ac741 (#1012, 2026-08-26).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: #1012 assumed an SQL comment is inert. psycopg2 %-formats the whole query string when params are passed, comments included. The existing tests could not see it: their MagicMock cursor's execute() ignores the SQL.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No change to what the query selects or filters. The comment moves into Python comments. The same class in build_lot_search_index.py step 1 is fixed the same way. The new test is the first check in tests/ that inspects SQL literals for placeholder hazards.

functions.name: fetch_dcp_setbacks
functions.input: An open psycopg2 connection, an LGA slug that may be None, an optional zone code, and raise_on_error.
functions.output: The controls dict unchanged in shape; registry_pdf_urls is again the {chapter_key: url} map for the council's active registry chapters with any URL, extended by CHAPTER_KEY_ALIASES.
functions.if_none: A None slug still returns None before any query. If the link-map query fails for any other reason it still degrades to an empty map inside its savepoint, as before.

functions.name: assign_overlays_for_lga
functions.input: An open connection, an LGA name from spatial_overlays and a dry_run flag.
functions.output: The same lot_search_index upsert; step 1 now runs instead of raising on the % in its SQL comments.
functions.if_none: dry_run or a zero lot count still returns the count before step 1, unchanged.

real_layer_exempt.scripts/conveyancing_db.py: Measured against the real database instead of a committed DB-marked test: the fixed fetch_dcp_setbacks on a normal read-only psycopg2 connection returned link maps of 2 chapters for penrith, 2 for cumberland, 3 for the_hills and 98 for marrickville (2026-09-13). The served layer is the Railway backend behind /api/dcp/structured-controls; post_merge.manual_verify checks it after deploy.
real_layer_exempt.scripts/build_lot_search_index.py: Step 1 writes lot_search_index for a whole LGA; running it here would rebuild production rows. The change removes comments only, and the scan plus psycopg2-style formatting covers the failure.

values: N/A - no stored value read or written changes; the queries select the same columns.

queries.purpose: Chapter-to-PDF URL map used to build every served numeric control's citation link
queries.where_clause: council = %s AND is_active = TRUE AND COALESCE(r2_public_pdf_url, council_url, council_page_url) IS NOT NULL

queries.purpose: Step 1 upsert of base lot rows into lot_search_index for one LGA
queries.where_clause: so.layer_type = 'zone' AND so.lga_name = %s AND c.geom IS NOT NULL

break_it.scenario: A later PR writes another explanatory comment with a percentage inside a parameterised SQL string, anywhere in scripts/ or services/.
break_it.what_happens: Without a check the query raises on every call; where an except swallows it the output silently degrades, as here.
break_it.how: test_no_stray_percent_in_parameterised_sql scans every execute()/executemany() literal with params and fails naming file and line.

break_it.scenario: The stray % is in an f-string or a string built in a variable before execute().
break_it.what_happens: The scan only reads string literals passed directly, so it would not flag it.
break_it.how: Not mitigated, and stated in the test docstring. fetch_dcp_setbacks itself is also covered behaviourally by the psycopg2-style formatting test, which does not depend on how the string is built.

break_it.scenario: A correct LIKE '%Road%' pattern in a parameterised query.
break_it.what_happens: psycopg2 would raise on it too, so flagging it is right; the fix is %%.
break_it.how: test_detector_flags_like_wildcard_with_params pins that it is flagged; test_detector_allows_escapes_and_placeholders pins that %% and %(name)s are not.

break_it.scenario: A query with no params, or sqlite's ? paramstyle, legitimately contains a literal %.
break_it.what_happens: A naive scan would fail the build on correct code (services/council_validation_service.py and scripts/zone_verification_suite.py use sqlite with LIKE '%...%').
break_it.how: Calls without params, with params=None, and sqlite ? queries without %s are skipped; a test pins all three.

break_it.scenario: The link-map query fails for a different reason after this fix (a renamed column, a lost connection).
break_it.what_happens: The savepoint except still swallows it: numbers are served with no link and only a warning is logged, exactly the silence that hid this for 18 days.
break_it.how: Not changed here: the degrade-to-empty design is deliberate so a citation failure never takes the controls down. Stated so the post-merge check watches the served output, not the log.
break_it.repro: curl -s 'https://verify.plotdetect.com.au/api/dcp/structured-controls?council=penrith&dev_type=dwelling_house' | python -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(sum(1 for c in d['categories'] for x in c['controls'] if x['pdf_url']))"

break_it.scenario: The new behavioural test passes because its fake returns the map even when execute() raises.
break_it.what_happens: A test that cannot fail would give false confidence.
break_it.how: Observed red: the same fake run against origin/main's conveyancing_db.py returned registry_pdf_urls {} (the except path), so the assertion on the map fails there.
break_it.repro: git show origin/main:scripts/conveyancing_db.py > /tmp/cdb.py and run the test body against it (see falsifiable_check.observed_red)

post_merge.db_reset: No schema or data change in this PR.
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes: after the backend deploys, GET https://verify.plotdetect.com.au/api/dcp/structured-controls?council=penrith&dev_type=dwelling_house must return controls with a non-null pdf_url (was 0 of 12), and council=cumberland&dev_type=residential_flat_building must link the 0.25 visitor rate to the Cumberland Part G PDF.
